title: Where the sources on Jaipur blue pottery differ
description: Two disagreements between the sources on Jaipur blue pottery: the year of its GI tag, and who first brought the craft to Jaipur.

summary: The year of the GI tag
Who brought blue pottery to Jaipur

u0001.text: Features and the GI documents disagree on when the GI came and on who brought the craft to Jaipur.

u0004.text: Man Singh I first brought blue and white to Jaipur

u0005.text: Ram Singh II introduced it from Delhi and Khurja

C059.text: The GI application says Man Singh I was the first to bring the art of blue and white to Jaipur, after his dealings with the Mughals and campaigns in Afghanistan.

quotes.quote: Man Singh I was the first to bring the art of blue and white to Jaipur subsequent to his interactions with the Mughals and through his campaigns in Afghanistan.

C062.text: Impart says Ram Singh II, ruler of Jaipur, introduced blue glaze pottery to Jaipur from Delhi and Khurja.

quotes.quote: Introduced in Jaipur from Delhi and Khurja by the ruler of Jaipur, Ram Singh II

C139.text: Urvashi Dev Rawal's feature reports that blue pottery is historically linked to Jaipur and got the geographical indication tag in 2006.

quotes.quote: it is historically linked to Jaipur and even got the Geographical Indication or GI tag in 2006.

C141.text: Impart says Jaipur's blue glaze pottery received a GI tag in 2008, while workshops making similar wares have cropped up elsewhere, such as Chinhat near Lucknow.

quotes.quote: Jaipur's blue glaze pottery received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2008, and while the industry remains protected in Jaipur, several other workshops producing similar wares have cropped up in regions such as Chinhat near Lucknow in present-day Uttar Pradesh.
